title: AxiomZero Investigative Dossier — Commercial Surveillance, Cloud Contracts, and Military-Tech Human Capital
lead: Test whether the supplied claims about Israeli military-intelligence technology, Western cloud contracts, commercial acquisitions, veteran employment, and surveillance describe documented facts or inferential leaps. The case treats each lead as a hypothesis; it does not presume unlawful access, algorithm transfer, foreign control, or a threat from an individual’s service history.
journalist: AXIOM Journalist / AxiomZero Special Investigations Division

claims.statement: Microsoft’s September 25, 2025 statement says it disabled specified services for an Israeli Ministry of Defense unit after a review; it does not endorse every allegation in press coverage.

claims.notes: Company primary statement is the controlling source for what Microsoft itself said; confidence labels from AXIOM are heuristic, not a legal or truth determination.

claims.statement: Drop Site News reported a compiled count of more than 1,400 Israeli intelligence veterans in U.S. technology; this is a media-reported count, not an official, independently audited roster.

claims.notes: The count’s methodology, duplicate resolution, job status, service history, reserve status, and role sensitivity require independent validation.

claims.statement: The record assembled for this AXIOM test does not establish that Wiz, CyberArk, Wix, Base44, Cato Networks, or another named commercial product contains a foreign-intelligence backdoor or shares client data with a foreign government.
claims.notes: A bounded non-finding about this record, not proof that no risk exists. No penetration tests, source-code review, access audit, or classified evidence was available.

claims.statement: The supplied leads naming “Eagle Mission,” a “Keshet” hardware-sabotage unit, a “Noisy Message” system, and direct battlefield-algorithm commercial spinoffs remain unverified in this case.
claims.notes: No reliable primary record or independent corroboration was available in the materials reviewed. Do not repeat as fact.

open_questions: Obtain and authenticate Microsoft’s full review record and the relevant Azure subscription, data classification, and service logs; identify precisely what Microsoft confirmed and what it did not inspect.

Obtain the complete Project Nimbus master agreement, schedules, security addenda, legal-request procedures, suspension clauses, and formal Google/Amazon/Israeli government responses; have qualified counsel assess the reported clause.

For each military AI system described in reporting, locate original military documentation, system specifications, operational directives, and right-of-reply records; distinguish decision support from automated target approval.
Verify the current legal status and closing terms of the Google–Wiz, Palo Alto–CyberArk, and Axon–Carbyne transactions using current SEC filings and official closing notices.

Test alleged commercial algorithm transfer only through provenance evidence (patents, source-code history, technical documents, testimony, or documented personnel projects), not through shared geography or alumni status.

For emergency-call platforms, obtain product specifications, PSAP procurement contracts, privacy impact assessments, retention/deletion rules, vendor access logs, and independent security audit results for each jurisdiction.

Reproduce the reported intelligence-veteran count from a documented sampling frame, resolve duplicate/ambiguous identities, avoid collecting unnecessary personal information, and do not infer reserve status or coordinated access from public profiles.
Request comments from every named corporate party and source authors; record responses, denials, corrections, and non-responses without treating silence as admission.
notes: AXIOM real-world stress test. Direct URL retrieval was blocked by this execution environment for several reporting and corporate pages; search results supplied article metadata and summaries, but publication requires a human to retrieve and verify the linked originals, underlying records, dates, quotations, and responses. No target systems were probed and no private data was collected. Confidence and source-quality scores are software heuristics only. The supplied dossier claims are leads, not evidence.
